notes.claim: A function's domain is the set of values allowed for the input, and its range is the set of values the function takes as output.
The domain includes the real inputs that would not cause an undefined operation, such as dividing by zero or taking the square root of a negative number.
A 12 mA signal on a 4 to 20 mA loop from a differential-pressure cell is 50% pressure difference but 71% flow, because the square root of 0.5 is 0.707.
The SQA HN Engineering Mathematics unit expects learners to identify the domain, range and asymptotes of a given function.
